titulo: The gate: the Telegram bot, with one owner
lead: Telegram is the simplest gate: you create the bot in two minutes and get a token. That token is the key to the gate. Whoever has the token controls the bot, and anyone can message a bot. That's why this lesson is half creation and half protection.
objetivo: create the bot with @BotFather, store the token only in .env, and set the assistant to respond only to you.

aprende.t: Why the token stays only in .env and out of Git
How the channel talks to Telegram (long polling)
Why the bot should accept messages only from its owner

hero_alt: Hands holding a phone with a messaging app open to a conversation.

nos.detalhe: Telegram’s official bot for creating bots. Send /newbot, choose a name and a @username (ending in bot), and you’ll get the token.
A string of numbers and letters. Whoever has the token controls the bot. It goes only in .env (or in the encrypted vault the plan calls for), never in code, a screenshot, or a commit.
The channel keeps asking Telegram if a new message has arrived. It doesn’t need a public address. It splits replies longer than 4096 characters and refuses to start without a token, by design.

itens.t: List of who can talk to it

nos.detalhe: Anyone who finds your bot’s @username can message it. Without a list of who can talk to it, anyone can chat with your Jarvis and use its tools.

secoes.volta: Replies go back to the same chat
secoes.legenda: INTELECTO was designed for one user. A Jarvis with access to your machine is powerful, and that’s exactly why it deserves care.

secoes.titulo: Create and protect it, step by step

texto: On Telegram, search for @BotFather (the official one, with a verified badge) and send /newbot.
Choose the name shown in the conversation and the @username, which must end in bot. It will reply with the token.

exemplo.texto: Use the name from your meu-jarvis.md. The @username can be the name + _bot.

texto: Paste the token on a line in the project folder’s .env, as you learned in step 1.
Check that .env is in .gitignore. Bots find exposed keys on GitHub quickly.

exemplo.texto: The token doesn’t appear in any file other than .env.

passos.sub: List of who can talk to it
texto: When you build it (lesson 4), ask the agent to have the bot reply only to your Telegram user and ignore everyone else.
In the vault (lesson 7), you’ll see why this matters even more when the assistant runs commands.

exemplo.texto: The bot replies only to my Telegram user; messages from other people are ignored and logged.

texto: A token in a screenshot, group, or commit has leaked. Don’t delete it and hope for the best: generate a new one in @BotFather and replace it in .env.
The old token stops working, and whoever got it loses access.

exemplo.texto: /mybots → choose the bot → API Token → generate a new one.

secoes.sub: Replace the text between < > with your token. Never paste the token here in the course or in a chat.

blocos.rot: Terminal · check that .env does not get pushed
Terminal · look for the token outside .env
blocos.conteudo: grep -rn "<the first 6 characters of the token>" . --exclude=.env

abas.html:
grep shows the .env line in .gitignore.

git status does not list .env.

The search for the start of the token finds nothing outside .env.

If git status shows ?? .env, the line is missing from .gitignore: add it before any commit.

If the search finds the token in another file, delete it there and generate a new token in @BotFather.

exercicios.texto: Create the bot in @BotFather with /newbot and save the token in the project's .env file.
exercicios.pronto: you have the token, and it does not appear in any file besides .env (the search in the third block finds nothing).

exercicios.titulo: E2b · Write down the sole owner's request
exercicios.texto: In your meu-jarvis.md, add the rule: it only responds to me on Telegram.
exercicios.pronto: the rule is written down and will go with the build request in lesson 4.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Where can the bot token appear?
opcoes: Only in .env (or the encrypted vault), outside Git.
In the README, as a reminder.
In the team group, so everyone can test.
perguntas.explica: Whoever has the token controls the bot. It belongs only in .env, which is in .gitignore; anywhere else, treat it as leaked and replace it.

perguntas.p: Why does the bot need a list of people who can talk to it?
opcoes: Because anyone can message a bot and use your assistant.
It doesn't need one: bots are private.
perguntas.explica: A Telegram bot is public to anyone who finds its @. Without the list, a stranger can talk to your Jarvis and use its tools.

perguntas.p: Your token appeared in a screenshot you posted. What should you do?
opcoes: Delete the post and move on.
Generate a new token in @BotFather and replace it in .env.
perguntas.explica: Deleting the post does not undo the leak. Generating a new token invalidates the old one; anyone who copied it loses access.
